title: National job openings and voluntary mobility cooled after 2022 while hiring remained lower
source_unit: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey national total-nonfarm establishment rates

denominator.unit: monthly seasonally adjusted JOLTS rate observations

job_openings_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

hires_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

quits_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

layoffs_and_discharges_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

total_separations_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

observations.method: Arithmetic mean of 12 BLS seasonally adjusted monthly national JOLTS rates; rates retain their BLS-specific denominators and are not converted into individual probabilities.
observations.uncertainty: Establishment-survey estimates are subject to sampling error, revisions, seasonal-adjustment updates, and coverage limits; annual means summarize monthly rates rather than unique workers.
observations.subgroup: Total nonfarm establishments; no worker demographic or occupation subgroup in this national series.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 2020 average spans the pandemic labor-market shock and should not be read as a normal baseline or a direct measure of worker welfare.

observations.counterinterpretation: The peak openings and quits rates can represent labor reallocation after reopening rather than a durable bargaining regime.

observations.uncertainty: Aggregate rates do not establish individual job quality, control, pay, or household consequences.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower quits may indicate reduced outside options, but may also reflect worker preference, retirement, sector composition, or measurement limits.

observations.uncertainty: 2025 values may be revised; the aggregate does not identify who bore the adjustment or whether worker control changed.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower quits rate is not alone evidence of worsening work conditions or a broad loss of bargaining power.

related_sources.claim: BLS field definitions specify the meaning and rate denominators for JOLTS measures.
related_sources.access_boundary: Definitions do not provide worker-level motivations, outcomes, or household linkage.

boundary: This record establishes an aggregate establishment-based labor-market context. It does not establish worker bargaining power, job quality, pay, schedule control, household security, political meaning, or a causal effect of any labor-market condition.
